questions.q: What is the purpose of the Receivables to Ledger Reconciliation Report?
options: To calculate customer aging buckets
To release invoice holds
To confirm that the Receivables subledger and the GL control account agree, broken out by transaction category
To format payment files for the bank
questions.explain: The report (run after Prepare AR to GL Reconciliation) confirms agreement between Receivables and GL, isolating any gap by category rather than leaving just one unexplained total.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the $9,000 gap at Harbor & Vance Logistics?
options: AutoInvoice rejected a transaction
A customer receipt was misapplied
The period was never opened
A manual journal was posted directly to the AR control account in GL instead of being entered as a Receivables transaction
questions.explain: A $9,000 manual journal was posted straight to the AR control account in GL, bypassing Receivables entirely, so the subledger never reflected it.

questions.q: Why is a direct journal to the AR control account a classic cause of AR-to-GL reconciliation breaks?
options: Because it changes the GL balance without the corresponding Receivables transaction ever being created, so the two totals diverge
Because it always represents fraud
Because it is technically impossible in Oracle Fusion
Because it automatically triggers AutoInvoice
questions.explain: A direct journal changes only the GL side; since it bypasses the subledger, the Receivables total and the GL control account total no longer agree.

questions.q: What was the correct resolution, given that the $9,000 adjustment itself might have been a legitimate correction?
options: Leave the direct journal in place since the amount was correct
Reverse the direct GL journal and enter the equivalent adjustment as a proper Receivables transaction
Delete the Receivables aging report instead
Increase the reconciliation tolerance to absorb the difference
questions.explain: The fix addresses where the adjustment was entered, not whether it was needed — reversing the direct journal and re-entering it through Receivables lets it flow through the subledger properly.

questions.q: What recommendation does the resolution note make to prevent this type of break from recurring?
options: Disable the AR control account entirely
Stop running the reconciliation report
Route all AR balance corrections through Receivables transactions rather than direct journals to the control account
Require GL users to get sign-off from Oracle support before any journal
questions.explain: The note recommends that GL users enter AR-related corrections as Receivables transactions instead of posting directly to the control account.
